historical_record.description: An electronic equipment factory at 1150–1152 Mission Street was torn down between 1959 and 1969, and the ground became a parking lot.

In October 1979 the site of a proposed Greyhound bus terminal held a package express facility, the vacant Atlanta Hotel and an electrical supply building, all to be demolished; the appeal of the requirement for an environmental impact report was continued.
An existing surface-level parking lot containing 168 spaces stood at the site.

The City Planning Commission adopted CEQA findings for the proposal to construct a new 23-story, 235-foot building with approximately 246 dwelling units and ground-floor retail, replacing an existing surface-level parking lot.

The City Planning Commission approved as amended, under Section 309 and for exceptions, the construction of a new 23-story, 235-foot building with approximately 246 dwelling units and ground-floor retail.
The City Planning Commission approved conditional use authorization for a public storage garage for passenger vehicles in conjunction with the new 23-story residential building.

The City Planning Commission approved with conditions as modified the conditional use authorization to permit additional building square footage above the base floor area ratio for affordable housing units at 1160 Mission Street.
